call_points.text: FY27 capex guided at about ₹87 Cr, mainly for copper value-added, antimony and plastic recycling projects.
Value-added copper products expected to add about 2% to copper EBITDA margin once stabilised.
Copper anode line fully commissioned with both furnaces, installed capacity 1,600 tonnes per month.
Copper cathode Phase-1 (1,500 tonnes per month) on track for Q2FY27 commissioning.
Copper wire rod (600 tonnes per month) and busbar/profiles (1,500 tonnes per month) expected in Q3FY27.
Plastic recycling facility on six acres expected operational in Q3FY27 with about ₹15 Cr investment.
call_points.versus_prior: reiterated the Q3FY27 timeline and ₹15 Cr capex from memory

call_points.text: Ahmedabad JV trial production commenced; operations expected to stabilise in Q2FY27.
Kuwait investment machinery shipment delayed by West Asia conflict; contribution expected from Q3FY27 onwards.
Copper and copper products contributed 67% of Q1FY27 revenue, up from 55% in FY26.
EBITDA margin at 4% in Q1FY27 versus 5.8% a year ago and 3.5% in Q4FY26.
Inventory days about 55, debtor days about 19 and working capital cycle about 60 days as of June 2026.
About ₹20-30 Cr of raw material stuck at sea due to West Asia crisis; fully insured against war.
Normalized copper EBITDA expected to stabilize at ₹30,000 to ₹32,000 per ton excluding Q3 tailwinds and Q4 external headwinds.
Value-added copper products will incrementally add ₹22 to ₹45 per kg in EBITDA over baseline copper earnings.
FY27 volume growth guided at 10% to 15% for lead, while copper has potential to grow beyond 15%.
Q4 copper EBITDA hit by ₹18,000-₹18,500/t from formula drops and ₹6,000/t from shipping and fuel inflation.
Shipments from US and South America transshipping at UAE Jebel Ali port got stranded due to Hormuz geopolitical disruptions.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: Not Applicable
tax_litigation.status: Pursuant to the search conducted at 5 premises of Jain Metal Rolling Mills and its promoter on December 3, 2014, the Commissioner of GST & Central Excise has passed an order on September 30, 2021 alleging that the assessee has removed Lead Ingots from the Factory during the period March 2014 to November 2014 without payment of applicable Excise duty of Rs. 3,22,50,249 and non-payment of excise duty on Plastic recovered from Battery Scrap Rs. 26194 including interest. The same has been alleged by the department based on the Packing Slips which did not have corresponding Excise Invoices. Further, the department has alleged that applicable service tax has not been paid on the Packing and Forwarding charges. Appeal was filed by the Assessee before Customs, Excise and Service Tax Appellate Tribunal on January 12, 2022 and the matter is pending before CESTAT.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: Not Applicable
tax_litigation.status: It has been alleged by the department that Jain Metal Rolling Mills has availed CENVAT credit based on invoices during the month of June 2012 from Moral Alloys Private Limited although goods have not been actually received. Further to the personal hearing of the assessee, the Asst. Commissioner of GST & Central Excise has issued an order dated June 6, 2018 levying penalty of Rs. 37,96,211, being the excise duty on these invoice for which CENVAT credit has been availed by the assessee. The assessee has made an appeal against the same before Commissioner (Appeals) Central Excise during September 2018 and the matter is pending before Commissioner (Appeals). The assessee has made a pre-deposit of 7.50% of the demand for the purpose of filing the appeal.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: Not Applicable
tax_litigation.status: Jain Metal Rolling Mills had purchased TIN ingots from Malaysia Smelting Corporation, Malaysia and had availed preferential duty under Notification 46/2011. However, the Certificate of Origin issued in favour of Malaysia Smelting Corporation was revoked. Hence the department had raised duty demand of Rs. 1,33,53,434 on Jain Metal Rolling Mills. The Company had filed a writ petition before the Madras High Court to quash the show cause notice. However, the same was dismissed by the Madras High Court. Further to this, the Company filed an appeal before Commissioner of Customs (Appeal) which rejected the appeal. Subsequently, the Company has filed an appeal before CESTAT and the matter is pending.

The amount of demand is Rs. 92,19,535 (including 9,00,448 penalty amount). Jain Metal Rolling Mills has appealed the matter before GST Appellate Authority and the matter is pending.

guidance.statement: Management expects normalized copper EBITDA to stabilize at approximately INR32,000 to INR30,000 on a steady state basis.
Total capex for FY27 across value-added copper phase 2, antimony, plastic, Kuwait and Ahmedabad JV will be around INR115 to INR120 crores.
Lead volume growth expected in the range of 10% to 15%, while copper has potential to exceed 15%.
FY27 total capital expenditure outlay of approximately Rs. 87 crores.
Value-added copper products expected to add about 2% to copper EBITDA margin once stabilised.

entities.name: Jain CY Circular Solutions Private Limited
Ahmedabad joint venture with C&Y Group Investment Incorporation

operating_notes.text: Copper segment contributed 55% of total revenue in FY26.
Copper segment capacity utilization stood at 65%, lead at 97-100%, and aluminium at 35% in FY26.
Working capital cycle stood at 66 days as of March 2026 (inventory 62 days, debtors 18 days, creditors 14 days).
Copper anode production was about 600 tonnes in Q1FY27, sold since commissioning.
Copper EBITDA per tonne was ₹31,000 in Q1FY27 versus FY26 average of ₹36,000.
Inventory days about 55, debtor days about 19 and working capital cycle about 60 days as of June 2026.
Board approved altering MoA to include mining, mineral extraction (including coal), and automated vending/retail technology systems.

holders.name: MOTILAL OSWAL ELSS TAX SAVER FUND

timeline.summary: Jain Resource Recycling announced postal ballot voting results approving IPO fund utilization for loan repayment and executive remuneration.
Jain Resource Recycling filed its monitoring agency report for Q4 FY26, disclosing the regularisation of a ₹54 crore promoter loan repayment deviation via shareholder approval.
2026-05-14: Jain Resource Recycling reschedules Q4FY26 earnings call to May 18 due to technical issue
Jain Resource Recycling filed its statement of deviation or variation under Regulation 32 for Q4 FY26, confirming zero deviation in IPO fund utilisation.
Jain Resource Recycling held its Q4FY26 earnings call, guiding to normalized copper EBITDA of ₹30,000-₹32,000/t and ₹115-₹120 Cr FY27 capex.
2026-08-08: Jain Resource Recycling filed the transcript of its Q1FY27 earnings call held on August 4, 2026, reporting 76% YoY revenue growth to ₹2,725 Cr and guiding FY27 capex of about ₹87 Cr.
The Board approved expanding the company's business objects to include mining, mineral processing, and automated vending technology on October 15, 2026.
Jain Resource Recycling announced a postal ballot notice to seek shareholder approval for altering its MOA objects and appointing independent directors.
Jain Resource Recycling provided corporate guarantees of ₹150 Cr to secure working capital facilities for its subsidiary Jain Green Technologies.
